mainTopic: Leaving one kind of Torah learning for another; the משנה on how much written Torah supports each area of הלכה; the sources for היתר נדרים; and why הלכות שבת 'hang by a hair'
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous page. A woman who was forced may stay with her husband, unless he is a כהן. Then רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן each explain the פסוק 'there was no peace for one who went out or came in' as a warning against leaving one kind of Torah learning for another. A new משנה follows and sorts areas of הלכה by how much written Torah supports them. היתר נדרים 'flies in the air.' שבת, חגיגה and מעילה are 'mountains hanging by a hair.' דינין, עבודות, טהרות and עריות are well grounded. In the גמרא, four תנאים each offer a פסוק as a source for releasing vows. שמואל offers 'לא יחל דברו': he cannot break his word, but others can release it for him. רבא shows that every source except שמואל's could be teaching something else. The amud ends with the הלכות שבת: they are written in the Torah, so the משנה must mean details like רבי אבא's rule about digging a hole only for its dirt. The גמרא then asks how such details 'hang by a hair,' and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: One case is forced, the other willing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first answer: one source speaks of a woman who was forced (אונס), and the other speaks of a woman who acted willingly (רצון).
steps.simpleTranslation: [Here it is] when she was forced; there it is when she was willing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started on the previous page. Two sources seemed to disagree about whether the woman becomes forbidden to her husband, and the גמרא says they are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she was forced (אונס), she may stay with her husband, so the damage can be fixed. If she was willing (רצון), she becomes forbidden to him, so the damage cannot be fixed. Splitting the cases this way removes the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: force; she was forced against her will
here... there; a way to split two sources into two different cases

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a sentence. The first 'כאן' (here) and the question being answered appear at the end of the previous page.

phrases.english: [here it is] with force; there it is willingly.
phrases.notes: The opening word 'here' is at the end of the previous page. This finishes that sentence.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן בְּאוֹנֶס, כָּאן בְּרָצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to describe the same case and to disagree about whether the harm can be repaired.
steps.terutzMaskana: When she was forced, she stays permitted to her husband. When she was willing, she becomes forbidden to him.

steps.title: Both cases are forced: a כהן's wife versus a ישראל's wife
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: both sources speak of a forced woman. The difference is that one is married to a כהן and the other to a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that both speak of a forced woman, and it is still not difficult: here it is a כהן's wife, there it is a ישראל's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different way to solve the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when she was forced, a כהן's wife becomes forbidden to her husband, so that harm cannot be fixed. A ישראל's wife who was forced stays permitted to her husband. So the line between the two sources is drawn by who the husband is, not by whether she was willing.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say; introduces a second answer
and it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
the wife of an ordinary Jew (not a כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to solve the contradiction: (1) forced versus willing; (2) both forced, but a כהן's wife becomes forbidden while a ישראל's wife does not.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say
this one and that one both speak of force,
and it is not difficult:
here it is the wife of a priest,
there it is the wife of an Israelite.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא וְהָא בְּאוֹנֶס, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same contradiction that step 1 answered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the only way to explain the difference is forced versus willing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when both cases are forced, a כהן's wife becomes forbidden and a ישראל's wife does not.

steps.title: רב: leaving הלכה for מקרא brings no peace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'and for one who goes out and comes in there is no peace.' רב explains that it refers to someone who leaves the study of הלכה for the study of מקרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for one who goes out and comes in there is no peace.' רב said: once a person goes out from הלכה to מקרא, he no longer has peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new short topic. It quotes a פסוק, and רב reads it as a warning about leaving one kind of learning for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'going out' as leaving the study of הלכה (the משנה and גמרא) to study the verses themselves. Without the explanation of the תורה שבעל פה, a person cannot settle the law clearly, so he 'has no peace'.

keyTerms.meaning: the study of the law (the oral Torah)

phrases.english: "And to the one who goes out and the one who comes in there is no peace,"
Rav said:
once a person goes out
from matters of law to matters of Scripture —
he no longer has peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַיּוֹצֵא וְלַבָּא אֵין שָׁלוֹם, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about leaving Torah learning, connected to the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving the study of הלכה for the study of מקרא leaves a person without peace.

steps.title: שמואל: leaving תלמוד for משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains the same פסוק differently: it speaks of someone who leaves the study of תלמוד to study משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: this is someone who separates from תלמוד to study משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his own reading of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's view, even moving from תלמוד to משנה causes the loss of peace. The תלמוד explains the reasons for the laws, while the משנה gives the rulings without explaining them.

keyTerms.meaning: the study that explains the reasons behind the משנה
the short rulings of the תנאים

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
this is one who leaves Talmud for Mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: זֶה הַפּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the פסוק that רב explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even leaving תלמוד for משנה leaves a person without peace.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even from one תלמוד to another
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן goes the furthest: even leaving one תלמוד for another תלמוד brings no peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: even from תלמוד to תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the third and broadest reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion widens the warning. רב speaks of leaving הלכה for מקרא. שמואל speaks of leaving תלמוד for משנה. רבי יוחנן says that even switching between two kinds of תלמוד takes away a person's peace, since he must learn a new style.

keyTerms.meaning: from one תלמוד to another תלמוד

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'there is no peace for one who goes out and comes in': רב (from הלכה to מקרא), שמואל (from תלמוד to משנה), רבי יוחנן (even from one תלמוד to another).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
even from Talmud to Talmud.
phrases.notes: This seems to mean switching between the תלמוד of ארץ ישראל and the תלמוד of בבל, which have different styles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ מִתַּלְמוּד לְתַלְמוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading, broader than רב's and שמואל's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even switching from one תלמוד to another leaves a person without peace.

steps.title: משנה: releasing vows has almost no support in the written Torah
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. The laws of releasing vows (היתר נדרים) 'fly in the air' and have nothing to rest on in the written Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: the release of vows flies in the air and has nothing to lean on.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes how much of the written Torah stands behind different areas of the law, starting with releasing vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם may release a person's vow, but this power is not written clearly in the Torah. It comes from the oral tradition, with only a slight hint in the verses. That is why the משנה says these laws 'fly in the air'.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
releasing a person from a vow, done by a חכם
flying in the air; without a clear source

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a list of the different areas of הלכה and how strongly each one is rooted in the written Torah.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The release of vows —
fly in the air
and they have nothing to lean on.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֶיתֵּר נְדָרִים פּוֹרְחִין בָּאֲוִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of releasing vows have almost no direct source in the written Torah.

steps.title: שבת, festival offerings and misuse of sacred property hang by a hair
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. הלכות שבת, חגיגה and מעילה have a little Torah text but many laws, like mountains hanging by a hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The laws of שבת, festival offerings and misuse of sacred property are like mountains hanging by a hair, because they have little written text and many laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on to a second group of laws. These do have a source in the Torah, but the source is very thin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a middle level. היתר נדרים had almost nothing to stand on. These laws have a short text in the Torah that carries a huge amount of detailed הלכה. The picture is a huge mountain hanging from one hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Mountains hanging by a hair: a lot of law resting on very little text

phrases.english: The laws of Shabbat, festival offerings, and misuse of sacred property
are like mountains hanging by a hair,
for they have little written text and many laws.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת, חֲגִיגוֹת וְהַמְּעִילוֹת הֲרֵי הֵם כַּהֲרָרִים הַתְּלוּיִן בִּשְׂעָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list. After laws with almost no source, it moves to laws with a thin source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבת, חגיגה and מעילה rest on little text with many laws.

steps.title: Monetary law, Temple service, purity and forbidden relations are well grounded
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with laws that have solid Torah support: דינין, עבודות, טהרות וטמאות, and עריות. These are the core of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Monetary laws, Temple service, purity and impurity, and forbidden relations have something to lean on, and these are the very body of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the strongest group: laws that are clearly backed by the written Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has laid out three levels. First, laws with no real source (היתר נדרים). Second, laws with a thin source (שבת, חגיגה, מעילה). Third, laws with plenty of support. This last group is called the 'body' of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The service and sacrifices in the בית המקדש
They have something to lean on: a solid Torah source
The main body, the core, of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three levels: no source (היתר נדרים), a thin source (שבת, חגיגה, מעילה), and solid support (דינין, עבודות, טהרות, עריות).

phrases.english: Monetary laws and Temple service,
purity and impurity, and forbidden relations
have something to lean on,
and these are the very body of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַדִּינִין וְהָעֲבוֹדוֹת הַטְּהָרוֹת וְהַטְּמָאוֹת וַעֲרָיוֹת יֵשׁ לָהֶן עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's list with the best-grounded group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These areas have solid Torah support and are the core of the Torah.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר finds a hint for releasing vows in 'כי יפליא' written twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר says היתר נדרים does have a source: the words 'כי יפליא' appear twice in the Torah. One is for making a vow and one is for releasing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, they have something to lean on, since 'כי יפליא' is written twice. One expression is for forbidding, and one is for permitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by bringing a ברייתא. In it, רבי אליעזר disagrees with the משנה and says releasing vows does have a hint in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said היתר נדרים 'flies in the air.' רבי אליעזר points out that the same expression for making a vow is written twice. He reads the extra one as a hint to undoing the vow. So in his view, releasing vows rests on a פסוק after all.
steps.confusionAlert: In the גמרא, 'יש להם על מה שיסמכו' is about היתר נדרים, not the list of laws at the end of the משנה. These תנאים are disagreeing with the משנה's claim that releasing vows has no source.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
They have something to lean on,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the laws of releasing vows from the משנה, not the list right before it.

phrases.english: as it says: 'When he clearly utters,' 'When he clearly utters'
two times:
one utterance for forbidding,
and one utterance for permitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לָהֶם עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's opening claim about היתר נדרים and gives a Torah source for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled 'כי יפליא' hints that a vow can be both made and released.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: 'I swore in My anger,' then I took it back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע finds the hint in תהלים. 'I swore in My anger' shows that an oath made in anger can be taken back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: they have something to lean on, since it says 'which I swore in My anger.' I swore in anger, and I took it back.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the same ברייתא gives a different פסוק as the source for releasing vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע reads the פסוק to say the oath was made in anger and later taken back. This matches how vows are released: the person regrets what he said. So regret over an oath has a hint in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: I took it back, I changed my mind

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They have something to lean on,
as it says: 'Which I swore in My anger'
In My anger I swore, and I took it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לָהֶם עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different פסוק for the same claim that רבי אליעזר made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath made in anger can be taken back, which hints at releasing vows.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: 'whoever is of a willing heart'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings the פסוק 'כל נדיב לבו' as the hint for releasing vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק says: they have something to lean on, since it says 'whoever is of a willing heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives yet another פסוק as the source for releasing vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties a gift to a willing heart. The idea is that a pledge holds while the heart still wants it. If the person regrets it, there is room to release it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak says:
They have something to lean on,
as it says: 'Whoever is of a willing heart.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לָהֶם עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source for the same claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pledge depends on a willing heart, which hints that it can be released when the person regrets it.

steps.title: חנניה: 'I have sworn and I will fulfill it'
steps.stepSummary: חנניה, the nephew of רבי יהושע, brings the פסוק 'I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous laws' as the hint for releasing vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניה, the son of רבי יהושע's brother, says: they have something to lean on, since it says 'I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous laws.'
steps.whatsHappening: The fourth and last תנא in the ברייתא gives his own פסוק for releasing vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses fulfilling the oath. Reading it as a hint suggests that not every oath must be kept, so some oaths can be released. With this, four different תנאים have pushed back on the idea that היתר נדרים has no source at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Four תנאים in the ברייתא each find a פסוק that hints at היתר נדרים, pushing back on the משנה's claim that these laws 'fly in the air.'

phrases.aramaic: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Chananya, son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother, says:
They have something to lean on,
as it says: 'I have sworn, and I will fulfill it,'
'to keep Your righteous laws.'

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לָהֶם עַל מָה שֶׁיִּסָּמֵכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth source in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'I have sworn and I will fulfill' hints that some oaths need not be kept, meaning they can be released.

steps.title: שמואל's source: others can release the vow
steps.stepSummary: שמואל offers 'לא יחל דברו': the person himself cannot cancel his word, but others, meaning a חכם, can cancel it for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If I had been there, I would have told them that my source is better than yours. The פסוק says 'He shall not break his word.' That means he himself cannot break it, but others can release it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds one more source for היתר נדרים and says it is stronger than all the ones brought before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לא יחל' is read as 'he cannot release it himself.' That wording leaves room for someone else to release it. The גמרא explains why it is better: רבא will show that each of the other פסוקים could be teaching something else, while this one cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not break his word (from the פרשה of vows)
Others, meaning a חכם who can release the vow

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If I had been there,
phrases.notes: He means if he had been sitting with the חכמים who gave the earlier sources.

phrases.english: I would have said to them:
Mine is better than yours
as it is stated: "He shall not break his word"
he himself cannot release it,
but others can release it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, אָמְרִי לְהוּ: דִּידִי עֲדִיפָא מִדִּידְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth source after the four sources in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא יחל' teaches that he cannot release his own vow, but others can release it for him.

steps.title: רבא: only שמואל's source cannot be pushed off
steps.stepSummary: רבא says each source has a weakness except שמואל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Every one of them can be pushed off, except for שמואל's, which cannot be pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא judges all the sources. This line sets up the next steps, where he shows the weakness in each earlier source one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פירכא here means the פסוק could be teaching something else, so it is not a clear proof. רבא says only שמואל's פסוק has no other job.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a reason the proof does not hold

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes שמואל's פסוק the main source for התרת נדרים.

phrases.english: Rava said:
All of them have a refutation,
except for Shmuel's, which has no refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא, לְבַר מִדִּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּלֵית לֵיהּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with שמואל's claim that his source is better and announces that the others will be pushed off.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only שמואל's source holds up against every challenge.

steps.title: Pushing off רבי אליעזר's source
steps.stepSummary: 'כי יפליא' could be teaching רבי טרפון's rule that a נזירות vow needs a clear statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn it from רבי אליעזר, maybe the word is used the way רבי יהודה taught in the name of רבי טרפון. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי טרפון: Neither of them becomes a נזיר, because נזירות only takes effect with a clear statement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that the extra word 'יפליא' may not be hinting to releasing vows. It could be teaching a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר needed the doubled 'יפליא' for היתר נדרים. רבא says one of them could teach that נזירות needs a clear, certain statement (הפלאה). Then the word is already used up, and there is no proof for releasing vows.

phrases.english: For if it is learned from Rabbi Eliezer
perhaps it is used like Rabbi Yehuda
who spoke in the name of Rabbi Tarfon.
As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Tarfon:
Neither of them is a nazir,
phrases.notes: These are two people who argued, and each vowed to be a נזיר if he turned out right.

phrases.english: because nezirut only takes effect with a clear statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי מִדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר — דִּלְמָא כִּדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first example of רבא's claim that every source has a פירכא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אליעזר's source from the doubled 'כי יפליא'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word may be needed for רבי טרפון's rule that נזירות needs a clear statement.

steps.title: Pushing off רבי יהושע's source
steps.stepSummary: 'באפי נשבעתי' could mean 'I swore in anger and I will not take it back.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn it from רבי יהושע, maybe the פסוק means: I swore in My anger, and I do not go back on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads רבי יהושע's פסוק the opposite way, so it no longer hints to releasing vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע read 'in My anger' as a hint that an oath made in anger can be taken back. רבא says it could mean the oath stands even though it was made in anger. Since the פסוק can be read both ways, it is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

phrases.english: If it is learned from Rabbi Yehoshua
perhaps this is what it is saying:
"In My anger I swore"
and I do not go back on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ — דִּלְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second source to be pushed off.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק could mean the oath stands firmly even though it was made in anger.

steps.title: Pushing off רבי יצחק's source
steps.stepSummary: 'כל נדיב לב' could teach that a vow decided only in the heart counts, which disagrees with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn it from רבי יצחק, maybe the פסוק comes to reject שמואל's rule. שמואל said: If someone decided in his heart, he still has to say it out loud. The פסוק teaches that it counts even though he did not say it out loud.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that 'כל נדיב לב' could be teaching about vows made only in the heart, not about releasing vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A generous heart' could mean a gift decided in the heart is binding even without speech. That reading disagrees with a different rule of שמואל that a vow must be spoken. If the פסוק teaches that, it says nothing about releasing vows.
steps.confusionAlert: The שמואל quoted here is a different rule of his, about speaking a vow. It is not his source for releasing vows from step 13.

phrases.english: If it is learned from Rabbi Yitzchak
perhaps it comes to reject Shmuel's view.
For Shmuel said:
If one decided in his heart
he still must say it with his lips,
and this teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו.
phrases.english: that even though he did not say it with his lips, it counts.
phrases.notes: The words 'it counts' are not written, but the גמרא means them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק — דִּלְמָא לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third source to be pushed off.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יצחק's source from 'כל נדיב לבו'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק may teach that a vow decided in the heart is binding, against שמואל's rule that it must be spoken.

steps.title: Pushing off חנניה's source
steps.stepSummary: 'נשבעתי ואקיימה' could teach רב's rule that one may swear to keep a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you learn it from חנניה, the nephew of רבי יהושע, maybe the פסוק teaches what רב גידל said in the name of רב. For רב גידל said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a person may swear to keep a מצוה? As it says: 'I have sworn and I will fulfill it, to keep Your righteous laws.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes off the last source. The פסוק could be teaching that it is allowed to swear to do a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנניה read the פסוק as hinting to releasing vows. רבא says it could simply teach רב's law that an oath to keep a מצוה is valid and proper. With that, all four sources are pushed off, and only שמואל's 'לא יחל' remains standing.
steps.whatToRemember: All the earlier sources for התרת נדרים could be teaching other laws. Only שמואל's 'לא יחל דברו' (he cannot break it, but others can release it) has no refutation.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִדַּחֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: If it is learned from Chananya, the nephew of Rabbi Yehoshua
perhaps it is like what Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav.
For Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
From where do we know that one may swear to keep a מצוה?
As it is stated: "I have sworn and I will fulfill it,"
"to keep Your righteous laws."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדַּחֲנַנְיָה בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ — דִּלְמָא כְּרַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and last source to be pushed off, completing רבא's survey.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק may teach רב's rule that one may swear to keep a מצוה.

steps.title: Only שמואל's source survives
steps.stepSummary: רבא's review ends: every proposed source had a weakness except שמואל's, which has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: But שמואל's source has no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the list it reviewed in steps 15-18. Every other source was pushed aside, but שמואל's source still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the other verses could be read as teaching something else, so none of them proves the point. שמואל's verse could not be read another way. So it is the one real source for the idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a weakness that knocks down a proof

steps.whatToRemember: Out of all the suggested sources, only שמואל's has no weakness.

phrases.english: But Shmuel's source has no refutation.
phrases.notes: This finishes what רבא started saying in step 14, once the other sources were pushed aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל לֵית לֵיהּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's statement after the four rejections in steps 15-18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's source is the only proof without a refutation.

steps.title: One sharp pepper beats a basket of squash
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב נחמן בר יצחק) uses a folk saying: one strong proof is better than many weak ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רב נחמן בר יצחק: this is what people mean when they say, 'One sharp pepper is better than a basketful of squash.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a folk saying to sum up what we just learned. It does not add a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many weak sources are like a whole basket of bland squash. שמואל's single solid source is like one sharp pepper. Quality beats quantity.

keyTerms.meaning: As people say, a folk saying

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak:
This is what people mean when they say:
One sharp pepper is better
than a basketful of squash.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a folk saying to sum up the result of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One strong proof is worth more than many weak ones.

steps.title: But the laws of שבת are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the משנה's claim that the הלכות שבת hang by a hair, since they are written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned 'the laws of שבת.' But they are written in the תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item in the משנה. It challenges the idea that the laws of שבת have almost no source in the verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said some laws are 'like mountains hanging by a hair,' meaning they rest on very little text. But the ban on work on שבת is stated clearly in the תורה. So how can שבת be on that list?
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether שבת is in the תורה. Everyone agrees it is. The question is why the משנה describes its laws as hanging by a hair.

phrases.english: The laws of Shabbat.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which listed the laws of שבת among the 'mountains hanging by a hair.'

phrases.english: They are written!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכוֹת שַׁבָּת. מִיכְתָּב כְּתִיבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of הלכות שבת as 'hanging by a hair'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Laws that are written clearly in the תורה cannot be described as resting on almost no source.

steps.title: It refers to רבי אבא's ruling on digging for dirt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means details like רבי אבא's ruling: digging a hole only for its dirt is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the משנה is needed for רבי אבא's rule. רבי אבא said: someone who digs a hole on שבת but only needs the dirt is פטור for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 21. The 'hanging by a hair' part is not the basic ban on work. It is the fine details, like רבי אבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging is a forbidden kind of work. But if the person wants only the dirt and not the hole, he is פטור. A detail like this is not written in the verses, so it hangs by a hair.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a particular case

phrases.english: No, it is needed for the view of Rabbi Abba.
As Rabbi Abba said:
One who digs a hole on Shabbat
and needs only its dirt
is exempt for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, לְכִדְרַבִּי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: the משנה refers to the fine details, not the basic ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to say that all of שבת rests on little text.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only rules like רבי אבא's hang by a hair.

steps.title: Whose view is רבי אבא following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רבי אבא follows and answers: רבי שמעון's, who exempts a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רבי שמעון's, who said: a מלאכה that is not needed for its own sake is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא stands behind רבי אבא's ruling and gives an answer right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person here wants the dirt, not the hole itself. That fits רבי שמעון's rule that a מלאכה done for some other purpose is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden work done not for its own direct result

steps.whyThisMatters: מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is a central idea across הלכות שבת, and רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה disagree about it.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? With Rabbi Shimon, who said:
a labor not needed for its own sake
is exempt for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the source of רבי אבא's ruling from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view stands behind רבי אבא's exemption
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, who exempts a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה

steps.title: It can fit רבי יהודה too, because the digging ruins
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה could agree here, because digging a hole only for its dirt damages and does not build.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יהודה. In his cases, the person is building or fixing something. Here, he is ruining something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that רבי אבא must follow רבי שמעון. It shows the ruling fits רבי יהודה's view too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds a person חייב even for a מלאכה not needed for its own sake, but only when the act fixes or builds something. Digging a hole you do not want just damages the ground, so even רבי יהודה would say פטור.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא's ruling works for both תנאים: for רבי שמעון because the hole is not wanted, and for רבי יהודה because the act ruins rather than builds.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda:
there he is fixing,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the cases where רבי יהודה holds a person חייב.

phrases.english: here he is ruining.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that step 23's answer is the only possible one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim that רבי אבא must follow רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involves a destructive act, which even רבי יהודה would exempt.

steps.title: So what does 'mountains hanging by a hair' mean?
steps.stepSummary: Having given רבי אבא's ruling as the example, the גמרא asks what the משנה means by calling such laws 'like mountains hanging by a hair.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What, then, does the משנה mean by 'like mountains hanging by a hair'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words. It asks how רבי אבא's ruling shows that the laws of שבת are 'mountains hanging by a hair.' This line sets up the answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the משנה is speaking about details like רבי אבא's ruling. Steps 23-24 showed that this ruling can fit either רבי שמעון or רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא asks what the thin 'hair' is that holds up such a detail in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Like mountains, meaning many big laws
That hang, that are held up by
By a hair, meaning a very thin source in the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new topic. It still concerns the הלכות שבת from step 21. The example of רבי אבא's ruling still stands; the גמרא is asking how it hangs 'by a hair.'

phrases.english: What is meant by 'like mountains hanging by a hair'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כַּהֲרָרִין הַתְּלוּיִין בִּשְׂעָרָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling that רבי אבא's ruling fits either רבי שמעון or רבי יהודה, the גמרא asks how such a ruling is 'hanging by a hair.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What thin Torah source ('hair') holds up rulings like רבי אבא's, so that they count as 'mountains hanging by a hair.'
